# Command-reader fixed CLI oracle

These inputs, expected values and source journal writes were independently captured from the unchanged `check_command_reference.py` and `check_command_json_boundary.py`, using pinned CPython 3.12.15. The original Bluetooth `CommandReader` ran against private journal directories. The controlled candidate returned those original observations; it did not produce expectations from Rust. Provenance records original source hashes and interpreter details. The manifest pins both compressed and expanded corpus bytes.

The reference gate retains all 1,026 ordered reads and 381 returned commands. The JSON-boundary gate retains all 23 cases. Operation streams preserve every original request-file and source-journal write, including their ordering. The generic Bluetooth model and its arbitrary-input functionality remain pending; this replaces only the two fixed CLI gates. Live model/package hashes and the namespace-package absence contract fail closed before output creation if source policy changes. This deliberately replaces interpreter/import failures with an explicit source-drift guard, rather than claiming to reproduce Python execution failures.

`original-cases.json` records 69 whole original executions, including candidate failures, malformed/deep/non-UTF8 JSON, Python numeric equality, journal ownership, cached expectations, post-child source/binary mutations and report-writing phases. Eighteen independent argparse cases cover CLI admission. Raw-path captures cover inherited byte environment and streams, raw root/candidate/output names and an ASCII alias to a raw root. Source reporting preserves the imported root alias.

`actual-proof.json` records six fresh unchanged-original/native comparisons using the same freshly built `command_probe`: both gates with normal paths, raw paths and an ASCII source alias. Every file, directory, stdout and stderr byte matched. Native checkers ran with `PATH=/nonexistent`; the controlled shell launcher checked a raw inherited environment value and emitted invalid-UTF8 stdout/stderr before execing the actual candidate. This is Linux x86-64 evidence, not device or ARM validation. The source model remains retained and pinned.
